title: Gatekeeper workload policy
description: CPU 1:4 ratio and mclabels violations per team and namespace, from the daily Gatekeeper workload report (MAPCO-11868).

panels.title: CPU ratio: workloads
panels.description: Selected run, teams and namespaces, summed from the run's per-namespace summary lines. Shows 0 when the selected run has none in the filter, and "no run" when no run is selected.

targets.expr: sum(max by (namespace) (max_over_time({job="__REPORT_JOB__", run_id="$run", team=~"$team", namespace=~"$namespace"} | json type, rule, workloads | type="summary" | rule="cpuRatio" | unwrap workloads | __error__="" [$__range]))) or (0 * sum(count_over_time({job="__REPORT_JOB__", run_id="$run", namespace="_team"} [$__range])))

options.content: Last 14 days, one bar per UTC day with a report run, stacked per team. Each bar is the **last run of that day** per team: a same-day rerun replaces the earlier number, lower or higher, and is never added on top. A team with no violations shows 0 (no segment, hover for the value). Outlined bars: total of the selected teams. Days without a run (weekends, stack down, a skipped run) have no bar. A day's bar is drawn once the day is over (after 00:00 UTC); until then the **dots at the right edge** show the newest run per team, stacked like the bars (hover for the values). Filtered by team only.

panels.title: CPU ratio: workloads per team
panels.description: Last run of each UTC day per team, stacked: a same-day rerun replaces the earlier number. A team at 0 shows 0. Outlined bars: total of the selected teams. No bar on a day without a run. Dots at the right edge: the newest run per team, so today's run shows before its bar appears after 00:00 UTC.

panels.title: New at deploy: distinct workloads, previous 24 h
panels.description: Workloads that violated a workload rule when they were deployed (Gatekeeper admission log lines), counted once per workload and rule over the previous 24 hours, even when both the warn and the enforced constraint of a rule matched it. These are deploy-time warnings, not the backlog above. Filtered by namespace only: admission lines carry no team, and All namespaces includes namespaces no report run has seen. The hourly steps end at the last whole hour, so dots at the right edge show the same count for the 24 hours up to now: a deploy from the current hour shows there right away.

targets.expr: count by (resource_namespace, constraint_kind) (count by (resource_namespace, resource_kind, resource_name, constraint_kind) (count_over_time({k8s_namespace_name="gatekeeper-system"} | json process, event_type, constraint_kind, constraint_name, resource_namespace, resource_kind, resource_name | process="admission" | event_type="violation" | constraint_name=~"workload-.*" | resource_namespace=~"$namespace" [1d])))

options.content:
**What this shows.** The daily Gatekeeper workload report (chart `gatekeeper-constraints`, `dailyReport`) evaluates the live workload policies against every Deployment and StatefulSet and pushes each run to Loki (`job="__REPORT_JOB__"`). Slack and this dashboard read the same numbers. Pick a **run** (the latest is the default), **teams** and **namespaces**.

* **CPU ratio**: workloads with a container whose CPU limit is not exactly 4x its CPU request (or that has no request/limit). *Containers* counts the offending containers.
* **mclabels**: workloads whose Pod template mclabels violate the policy. **missing**: a required mclabel is absent. **invalid**: an empty value, an owner outside the allowed list, or `environment=undefined`. A workload can be both, so missing + invalid can exceed workloads.
* Teams come from `namespaceTeams` (e.g. dem-dev counts under 3d). **silenced** holds the namespaces with `silence: true`: they get no Slack message and are shown only here.
* **Fix**: set the CPU limit to 4x the request, and put the mclabels on `spec.template.metadata.labels`. **Exempt**: see the [chart README](https://github.com/MapColonies/helm-charts-new/blob/master/charts/gatekeeper-constraints/README.md#exemptions).
* Data exists only while the stack runs (Sun-Thu 04:00-16:00 UTC) and for the Loki retention (14 days). The trend shows the last run of each day, so a same-day rerun replaces the earlier number instead of adding to it.
